about: The generator of Cascade's documentation site: the pages of a sample pod, the specification, the term reference, and the unit-test pages, of which this is one. Nothing installs it: it runs when the site is built, and this page is for whoever changes the site or sends it a test report.

glossary.definition: the one sentence, under a package's name on its tests page, that says what the package is and who calls it; it is the `about` of the package's `spec.json`.
an adapter's own list of every source path of its format, each with a verdict: carried into a record, and as which vocabulary term, or not carried, and why.
the program that converts an export into records; `import` loads it on first use.
the part of a web address after `#`, which takes a reader to one place on a page: the `id` of a heading, a rule or an entry.

the closed section at the end of a package on a tests page, headed "Build and packaging", for the cases of a file or capability that a package's `spec.json` lists under `build`, checks of how the package is built; it is not part of the specification.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
one thing a package does for whoever calls it, named as a developer would search for it, with its API after a dot: the top level of a tests page, and the outermost `describe` of a test file.
one test as a report records it: its name, whether it passed, failed or was skipped, and how long it took. On a tests page a case is a leaf: it completes the sentence "it …".
one line of the Choice table of a decision note: a thing that was decided, the prior art, and what the vocabulary does, which names the rule the decision led to.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
what one run of the vocabulary's features against a runtime found: for each example, passed, failed or not run. The run writes them in EARL.
the page the site makes from an adapter's accounting: each source path beside the vocabulary term it is carried as, and the source paths that are not carried.
Common Test Report Format, an open JSON format for test results (ctrf.io); the site writes each suite's results in it beside the page, for an agent.

a Markdown file in the vocabulary's `decisions/` folder that settles one design question: a Choice table of what was decided, and a Why section whose paragraphs each give the reason for a Choice row. A rule names the note and the Choice row that ruled it.
the SHA-256 hash of a text, written in hexadecimal; a few of its first digits tell apart two things of one name.
a `/** … */` comment directly above a `describe` or a test; the tests page shows it as that level's description.
the `## Docs` section a repository's README opens with: links into the site, the front page first.
Evaluation and Report Language, a W3C format for test results as Turtle; conformance results are written in it.
under a rule in a feature, one worked scenario: a pod made a certain way, and what must then be true of it. A conformance run passes or fails each.
a file of the vocabulary that states its rules on one subject, each with examples, in Gherkin, such as `runtime/arrivals.feature`; a kit has one of its own.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
a function the site's build calls last, with every file the sections wrote, which returns more files made from them, such as an index.
the site's `index.html`: a "Find your way" table of what a reader may have come for, and a list of the project's repositories.
a named reason a source path is not carried, or is carried in part, such as "only the first note is carried"; an adapter lists its gaps in a file of its own.

the words a package's tests use in one sense, each with a one-sentence definition, listed in the package's `spec.json` and shown under its about line; a term may have aliases, other forms of the word that link to the same definition.
`guide/AGENTS.md` of the cascade-runtime package: the document for a developer, or a coding agent, who is building an app on a pod. The site shows it as the API page and copies it as `AGENTS.md`.
a web-style identifier, such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#allergen`; every vocabulary term, record and view entry is named by one.
an XML format for test results that most test runners can write; each runner fills it in its own way.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
one of the five things `runtime/the-kit.feature` requires of a replay of a kit's story, numbered 2 to 6, such as check 3, "every file conforms to the shapes". Check 1 is that every example passes.
a choice of which judgments count when a question is answered: `everyday` is the default, and `export` is stricter, for records sent elsewhere.
a heading of a tests page that holds cases or other levels: a capability, or a situation under it. In a test file it is a `describe`.
a Markdown file at a site's root, in the form llmstxt.org proposes, that lists the site's main links in groups for a language model to read.
the part of a runtime that compares a pod's records and writes a Same for those its rules find to be one thing, such as one allergy reported by two sources.
a query the vocabulary carries under a name, such as `pod/My active allergies`.
the shared start of the IRIs of one vocabulary, such as `http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/`, which a prefix such as `foaf:` stands for.

one folder `packages/<name>/` of a repository, with its own `test/` and `spec.json`: a tests page shows each as one top-level group of capabilities; a repository with no `packages/` is one package named for it.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
the JUnit file one run of a repository's tests wrote; the site reads the newest from `main`.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
a line of the front page's "Find your way" table: one thing a reader may have come for, such as "build an app", and the links that serve it. Each section says which row its links go in.
a numbered requirement in the vocabulary that every runtime must meet, such as A14 in `runtime/arrivals.feature`; a heading on this page links the rules its API reaches.
the program that runs a repository's tests and writes the report: node:test, pytest, vitest or nextest.
software that reads and writes pods as the vocabulary requires; this package is one.
one part of the site, such as the term reference or the specification: the files it writes, among them its entry page, and the links it lists for the front page.
the vocabulary's requirements on what a record, a judgment or a file of a pod must state, written in SHACL, the W3C language for checking data.
the second level of a tests page: the function under test, written as code, or a circumstance beginning "when", "given" or "with".
a name made fit for an address: lowercase letters and digits, with one hyphen for each run of anything else.
where a value sits in a record of a source format, written as a path such as `/code/coding/code` in FHIR.
the file `test/spec.json` of a package: its about line, its capabilities in the order the page shows them, its glossary, and the files and capabilities it lists under `build`, which are build checks.
the vocabulary's features, read as the rules a pod and a runtime must meet; the site shows them under `spec/`.
cascade-starter-kit: the app template that `create-cascade-app` makes, and the `try/` page that runs one in a browser.
one repository's tests, as `packages/site/test-suites.json` lists them: where its newest report is found and which runner wrote it.
the strip that stays at the top of a tests page: the package, the commit, the counts of passed, failed and skipped cases, the run time and three buttons.
the page of the site, at `terms/`, that has an entry for every vocabulary term.
where a repository's test files sit when that is not `test/` or `tests/`, as `test-suites.json` gives it in `tests`, ending in "/"; the page leaves it off the names of the files.
the page of one repository's test results, read as a specification.
a W3C text format for writing statements in the vocabulary's terms; `pod.enter()` and `pod.judge()` take it.
what an accounting says an adapter does with a source path: carried, carried in part, no home in the vocabulary, ignored, consumed in reading the record, or redundant with another source path.

a pod's records of one kind, such as medications, as its judgments leave them: one line for each thing however many sources reported it. A named question such as `pod/My medication history` returns a view's rows.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
cascade-vocabulary, the project that defines the words health data is written in, the requirements every pod meets, and a set of ready-made questions.
one word the vocabulary defines, such as `cascade:allergen`: a class, a property or a named value, named by an IRI.
